articles.title: Amid Higher-for-Longer Mortgage Rates, Multifamily Pros Find a Silver Lining
articles.narrative: This article analyzes how persistently high mortgage rates, which have remained elevated since late 2022 and spiked to nearly 8% in late 2023, are creating a silver lining for the multifamily and single-family rental sectors. With homeownership becoming significantly more expensive than renting, demand for rental housing is surging as households are priced out of buying. This shift, coupled with a contracting pipeline for new home construction, is expected to drive healthy rent growth and increased deal flow for multifamily assets, which also benefit from shorter lease terms allowing for quicker repricing in an inflationary environment.

articles.title: Reuben Brothers’ Jordana Yechiel On the Firm’s Big Bet on Century City
articles.narrative: Reuben Brothers is making a significant investment in Century City, Los Angeles, transforming the area around the Fairmont Century Plaza hotel and Park Elm condominiums into a luxury-driven, mixed-use destination. The firm's strategy involves layering in residential, experiential, and luxury offerings, including restaurants, galleries, wellness facilities, and a revamped public plaza. This approach is driven by a belief that the way people want to live in Los Angeles has shifted, with a desire for more integrated, round-the-clock environments, drawing inspiration from successful transformations like Dubai's International Financial Centre. The firm is focused on curating tenants and amenities to create a holistic destination rather than simply maximizing occupancy or rent.

data_points.notable_features: Features the Fairmont Century Plaza hotel, Park Elm condominiums, and a vertiport for eVTOL services.

articles.title: Downtown D.C. Office Conversion Secures $176M Loan, New Majority Partner
articles.narrative: A major office-to-residential conversion project in downtown Washington, D.C., has secured $175.6 million in construction financing and a new majority partner. MetLife Investment Management acquired a 72% stake in the redevelopment of 1990 K Street NW for $58.7 million. The project, which will be rebranded as 1999 Eye Street NW, is part of the city's Housing in Downtown program, offering a 20-year tax abatement for such conversions.

data_points.notable_features: Mixed-use property with market-rate apartments, affordable units, student housing, and retail space.
data_points.project_notes: The 2.6-acre site was previously acquired for $55.8 million in 2001. Demolition began in September 2025. The project benefits from D.C.'s Housing in Downtown program, which provides a 20-year tax abatement for office-to-residential conversions.

articles.title: Geoff Mason Promoted to U.S. Chief Operating Officer of Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield
Sagehall Picks Up Chetrit Organization’s 428 Broadway for $47M
articles.narrative: Sagehall, a New York City-based private real estate investment firm, has acquired the six-story office building at 428 Broadway in Manhattan's SoHo neighborhood for $47 million. The seller was a partnership between Chetrit Organization and American Industrial. The property faced distress after its anchor tenant, WeWork, filed for bankruptcy in 2023, leaving the building largely vacant. The sale follows a foreclosure process initiated by LoanCore Capital Credit, with the mortgage debt later transferred to an entity of the selling partners, who then took ownership through a foreclosure auction to facilitate the sale.

data_points.project_notes: The Chetrit Group originally purchased the property in 2005 for $22.5 million. The building became 96% vacant after WeWork's bankruptcy in 2023. LoanCore Capital Credit initiated foreclosure actions in 2024 on approximately $200 million in loans, which included this property and 1 Whitehall Street. The mortgage debt on 428 Broadway was transferred to C&AI Soho Holding, an entity of the Chetrit Organization and Donics, in late 2025, which then took ownership via foreclosure auction.

articles.title: JLL Arranges $78.7M Loan for Refinancing of East Dallas Apartment Community
articles.narrative: JLL has arranged a $78.7 million refinancing loan for The Flynn at Live Oak, a newly constructed 327-unit apartment community in East Dallas. The loan was secured through Blue Owl Capital on behalf of the ownership partnership between Conor Commercial Real Estate and Globe Corp. The five-story property features a strong amenity package designed to appeal to residents.

data_points.notable_features: Amenities include a pool, outdoor courtyards with fire pits and grilling stations, a sky lounge, fitness center with outdoor yoga space, coworking lounge and a grab-and-go convenience store.

articles.title: Alterra Acquires 23.5-Acre Industrial Outdoor Storage Portfolio in San Antonio
articles.narrative: Alterra IOS has acquired a portfolio of six industrial outdoor storage (IOS) facilities, totaling 23.5 acres, in the greater San Antonio area. The portfolio includes five properties within San Antonio and one in the suburb of Schertz. These facilities offer a combined 172,141 square feet of warehouse space and are fully leased to a diverse tenant mix across various industrial sectors.

data_points.notable_features: Portfolio includes six industrial outdoor storage facilities with warehouse space.

articles.title: Summit RE Negotiates Sale of 14,895 SF Retail Strip Center in Midlothian, Texas
articles.narrative: Summit RE has facilitated the sale of Harvest Hill Town Center II, a 14,895-square-foot retail strip center in Midlothian, Texas. The property features a strong tenant mix, including national brands. The seller and buyer, along with the transaction price, were not disclosed.

articles.title: Marcus & Millichap Brokers Sale of 14,000 SF Medical Office Building in West Houston
articles.narrative: Marcus & Millichap has brokered the sale of a 14,000-square-foot medical office building in West Houston. The property, constructed in 2024, was approximately 40 percent leased at the time of sale. The undisclosed buyer intends to occupy the remaining vacant space.

articles.title: Portland Industrial Market Finds Stability as Supply Pressures Ease
articles.narrative: Portland's industrial market is transitioning into a more balanced phase, characterized by stabilizing port activity and a significant slowdown in new construction. This moderation in the development pipeline is expected to help the market absorb existing inventory and ease competitive pressures, despite elevated vacancy rates. Demand remains robust for modern warehouse and distribution facilities, particularly those under 50,000 square feet and located near major transportation corridors, driven by e-commerce, local manufacturing, and service businesses. Investment activity is anticipated to focus on well-located assets with strong logistics advantages and properties supporting advanced manufacturing, signaling a foundation for measured, long-term growth.

articles.title: Colliers brokers sale of medical outpatient facility in Eagan
articles.narrative: Colliers brokered the sale of Eagan Medical Center, a 43,419-square-foot medical outpatient facility in Eagan, Minnesota. The property, anchored by several specialty healthcare providers, was sold by Tareen Development Partners.

data_points.notable_features: Anchored by MNGI Digestive Health, Minnesota Urology, and Tareen Dermatology; offers ample surface and underground parking; conveniently located near Interstates 35E and 494.

articles.title: World Cup games kicked retail, restaurant sales up … but mostly for retailers with the right strategies and location
articles.narrative: A new report from Colliers and Placer.ai analyzes retail and dining patterns during the FIFA 2025 World Cup, concluding that proximity to venues alone did not guarantee a business boost. The study, "7 World Cup Lessons for Retail, Dining & Real Estate," found that the economic impact was highly localized, with the strongest gains concentrated around stadiums, Fan Fests, and commercial districts that actively integrated into the fan experience. Properties that performed best became part of the fan experience through strategic tenant mix, gathering spaces, or activations, rather than just relying on increased traffic. This suggests that for future mega-events, intentional connections between events and commercial districts are crucial for landlords and investors to maximize consumer spending.

articles.title: Winstead PC adds shareholder to Real Estate Development & Investments Practice Group in Houston
articles.narrative: McCall Grimes has joined Winstead PC's Houston office as a Shareholder in the Real Estate Development & Investments Practice Group. Grimes brings extensive experience advising sponsors, developers, and investors on various real estate and strategic transactions, including joint ventures, acquisitions, development projects, financings, and fund formations. His background includes serving as General Counsel for The Dinerstein Companies, a prominent multifamily and student housing developer, where he advised on nationwide transactions and investments.

articles.title: PREMIER Design + Build Group adds general superintendent in Columbus
articles.narrative: David Lewis has been appointed General Superintendent at PREMIER Design + Build Group, operating out of the firm's Columbus, Ohio, office. In this role, Lewis will oversee field operations for the company's projects in Ohio, focusing on project execution, safety, quality, and team development. He brings over 40 years of construction experience, including three decades in field management, with a track record of successfully delivering large-scale industrial and commercial projects.

articles.title: JLL Arranges Refi for Maine Self-Storage Asset
articles.narrative: JLL Capital Markets Debt Advisory team has arranged a five-year refinancing loan for a recently constructed self-storage facility in South Portland, ME. The loan was secured through a regional bank on behalf of the borrower, The Ardent Companies. The property, completed in 2022, has achieved high occupancy, reflecting the strong demand in one of New England's most robust self-storage markets.

data_points.notable_features: Features climate-controlled units with 24/7 access and is located just south of Portland International Jetport.
data_points.project_notes: Managed by Extra Space Storage Inc.

articles.market_intelligence: The trade area for the property includes over 125,000 households within a 30-minute drive, with average household incomes exceeding $133,000 in the surrounding area.

articles.title: BXP Acquires Boston-Area Office Buildings for $30M
articles.narrative: BXP, a Boston-based REIT, has acquired two office buildings in Waltham, MA, for a total of $30 million. The properties, located within the Bay Colony office park, were purchased from an affiliate of the Massachusetts Medical Society. This acquisition follows a recent rezoning of the area for multifamily development, aligning with broader efforts in Massachusetts to convert underutilized office spaces into residential units.

data_points.notable_features: Located within the Bay Colony office park; area recently rezoned for multifamily development.
data_points.project_notes: The acquisition included two buildings: 860 Winter St. for $17 million and 870 Winter St. for $13 million.

articles.title: Chicago/Midwest People & Company News, week of September 4, 2026
articles.narrative: Entre Commercial Realty recently facilitated the sale of a 25,000-square-foot industrial flex building in Spring Grove, Illinois. The multi-tenant property, situated on 2.29 acres, was fully leased at the time of the transaction. The sale involved representation from RD Strategic for the buyer and Entre Commercial Realty for the seller.

data_points.notable_features: Multi-tenant property divided into five units, fully leased at the time of sale.

articles.title: CEDARst Snags $80M Construction Loan for San Diego Apartments
articles.narrative: CEDARst Companies secured an $80 million construction loan for The Samuel, a 197-unit Class A multifamily development in San Diego's North Park neighborhood. The financing, arranged by JLL, will facilitate the construction of the eight-story building, which is expected to break ground in Q3 2026 and be completed by Q4 2028. The project will offer a mix of studio, one-, and two-bedroom units along with a comprehensive suite of amenities.

data_points.notable_features: Class A multifamily development with a pool, fitness center, co-working lounge, fire pits, game deck, and a rooftop sunset lounge with an outdoor kitchen.
data_points.project_notes: Construction is expected to begin in Q3 2026.

articles.title: Colliers Completes 67K-SF Industrial Lease in Maryland
articles.narrative: Colliers recently completed a 67,040-square-foot industrial lease at 4780 Winchester Boulevard in Frederick, Maryland. The landlord, Link Logistics, secured Senneca Holdings, Inc., a manufacturer of data center containment solutions, as the new tenant. The property's strategic location within a key Mid-Atlantic industrial corridor offers excellent connectivity to major East Coast population centers, which was a significant factor in attracting the new tenant.

data_points.notable_features: Located within a strategically positioned industrial corridor with immediate access to Route 15, I-70, and I-270, providing connectivity to Washington, D.C., Baltimore, and Northern Virginia.

articles.title: Georgia-Pacific Scraps Conversion Plans For Its Atlanta HQ
articles.narrative: Georgia-Pacific has halted its plans to convert a portion of its Atlanta headquarters into 400 apartments. The decision was driven by escalating construction costs and broader market challenges, making the residential conversion financially unfeasible at this time.

data_points.notable_features: Planned conversion of existing office space into residential units.
data_points.project_notes: Project halted due to rising costs and market challenges.

articles.title: Retailers Charging Ahead With EV Stations Despite Policy Pullback
articles.narrative: Despite a flattening in new electric vehicle (EV) sales in 2025, the used EV market is experiencing rapid growth, prompting retailers to continue investing in EV charging stations. This trend suggests that while initial adoption rates for new EVs may have slowed, the overall demand for EV infrastructure remains strong due to the expanding secondary market for these vehicles. Retailers are likely anticipating sustained long-term demand for charging solutions as more used EVs enter circulation.

articles.title: Passco Sells Buckhead Apartment Complex: The Atlanta Deal Sheet
articles.narrative: Passco Companies has sold a 345-unit apartment complex in Atlanta's Buckhead neighborhood to Orix USA, which plans to implement upgrades to the property. The transaction represents an 18% loss for Passco Companies on its original investment.

data_points.notable_features: Orix USA plans to implement upgrades to the property.
data_points.project_notes: Passco Companies sold the asset at an 18% loss on its original investment.

articles.title: Y'all Street Powers Trophy Office Momentum In Uptown Dallas
articles.narrative: Y'all Street is identified as a significant driver of top-tier office growth in Uptown Dallas, contributing to high rental rates and fostering new development projects in the area.

articles.title: Miami-Dade Overturns Mayor's Veto For 2.7M SF Kelly Tractor HQ Beyond Urban Development Boundary
articles.narrative: Miami-Dade County has approved the development of a new 2.7 million-square-foot headquarters for Kelly Tractor, overriding a mayoral veto. This decision allows for the construction of the facility outside the established Urban Development Boundary, a move that has faced opposition regarding its environmental and planning implications.

data_points.notable_features: Located beyond the Urban Development Boundary.
